_about: The narration of Scenario 2's narrated cut, draft 2 (S317 SkyCompass, 2026-10-02), voiced by Sierra. Sam, 2026-10-02: "write a script for the scenario 2 video for an ElevenLabs narrator. Keep it very simple and focused and see if you can select a female voice model to narrate and give her the name Sierra on the video as a sample", and "The music can drop to background level." One or two plain sentences per scene of the current Scenario 2 picture (the introduction's v7: the average allocation, the targets slide, December 30, 2026, the CPL funding page), about 330 words where draft 1 had 430. Every figure is the film's, read from the engine under the live config, md5 764fd264 (checked live 2026-10-02): $35,000,000; about $25 million to 118 institutions; the $150,000 to $400,000 range and the $213,901 average; 4,366.7 FTES statewide for each priority; 34.5 FTES for the average Access target. The voice says the figures in words and writes MAP as map, so the captions and the aligner read what she says. Draft 3 (S443, 2026-10-21): Sam's edits to every scene but Support, from his marked-up script (20261021_CPL_Funding_in_Motion_Narration_Script_Sierra.docx); the figures are the published Scenario 3's (about 4,269 FTES per priority, an average Access target of about 31.3 FTES).

engine.name: elevenlabs
engine._why: Bella is an ElevenLabs premade voice (always available, unlike a library voice, which its owner can withdraw): "warm, bright, and professional... Standard American accent... crisp diction and a deliberate, rhythmic pace". Sierra is the name the film gives her (Sam, 2026-10-02). One generation per scene through the ElevenLabs connector; each scene's `read` names its clip and generation, and `text_sha1` is the SHA-1 of the text it was read from. narrate.py brings every clip to one speech level, -20 dBFS RMS, 2 dB over the Kokoro read it replaces, so the score sits further back.

layout._why: The narrated cut paces each scene as its lead-in (the seam, its barrier and the first reveal), its clip, and its air; Sam, 2026-09-26: "slow down and lengthen the timing a bit to accommodate readability and narration."

scenes.text: Greetings CPL heroes! Here's how CPL Initiative funding works for your college.

cues.why: the name beneath the lockup, Narrated by Sierra
the title, CPL Initiative Funding: How It Works, letter by letter
the kicker, An introduction for colleges

scenes.text: Huge thanks to our Chancellor, Board of Governors and the legislature for appropriating thirty-five million dollars to support CPL. About twenty-five million goes directly to the colleges, while the remainder is funding CPL infrastructure and innovation projects.

cues.why: the kicker, One-time funding for 2026–27
cues.skip: the picture shows it before the $35,000,000 counter, and the voice names it after; the counter takes the cue

cues.why: the line, set aside by the state to help colleges build credit for prior learning
cues.skip: the voice says it about a second before the counter lands, and the picture needs 2.2 seconds of film before it; pinned, it would hurry the count, so the counter takes the cue and the line follows its words

cues.why: the counter lands on $35,000,000 as the voice says thirty-five million
the bar's first segment and its label, $25,240,308 directly to 118 institutions
the second segment and its label, $9,759,692 for statewide CPL projects and technology and two Chancellor’s Office positions

scenes.text: Each institution has a maximum allocation for the two-year period, with smaller colleges eligible for base funding of one hundred fifty thousand and larger colleges capped at four hundred thousand dollars. The average is about two hundred fourteen thousand.
scenes.air_why: The picture runs six seconds past the average marker (its bottom line, Smaller institutions are brought up to the base. The largest are held at the cap.), and the voice ends two seconds after naming the average; with the usual 0.8 s of air the marker and the cap led their words by 2.6 and 2.2 s.

cues.word: Each institution has a maximum allocation
cues.why: the heading, Every institution has a maximum allocation

cues.word: base funding of one hundred fifty thousand
cues.why: the range line, and the base, $150,000, at its left
the cap, $400,000
the Average allocation marker, $213,901, slides onto the range

scenes.text: Allocations are split between credit and noncredit shares, so all students are supported.

cues.why: the heading, The average splits in two
$213,901 splits into the credit share and the noncredit share, which count up
its bold sentence, Only noncredit outcomes count toward the noncredit share

scenes.text: Funding is based on two priority outcomes. The access priority counts all applied, or articulated, CPL units, whereas the completion priority counts transcribed CPL units. The Chancellor's Office will report on career attainment together with the infrastructure and innovation projects.

cues.word: Funding is based on two priority outcomes
cues.why: the heading, Two priorities carry the funding
the Access card, 50 percent and $12,620,154 statewide
the Completion card, 50 percent and $12,620,154 statewide
the reported card, Career attainment and innovation projects

scenes.text: Outcomes are measured in FTES and funding at half the FTES reimbursement rate, which totals four thousand two hundred sixty-nine FTES per priority statewide.

cues.why: the heading, How a target is set
the line, A priority's statewide funding, divided by its FTES reimbursement rate
cues.skip: the voice names the funding and the rate in one breath, and the picture needs 2.2 seconds between the line and the rate row while the funding counts up; pinned, the line led its words by 1.9 seconds, so the rate row takes the cue

cues.why: the rate row, $2,824.82: the $5,649.63 base rate times a factor of 0.5
the Access target lands on 4,366.7 FTES, the institutions’ targets added up
the line, Completion is set the same way: 4,366.7 FTES

scenes.text: Your college has its own target under each priority. Thirty semester units of CPL are counted as one FTES. For the average allocation, the Access target is about thirty-one FTES. Reach half the target, and your college qualifies for half the maximum funding. Colleges that achieve target for both priorities receive full funding.

cues.word: Your college has its own target
cues.why: the heading, Every priority has a target
the line, 30 semester units of CPL make one FTES, or 45 on a quarter calendar
the card, Priority 1 · Access · average allocation · target 34.5 FTES · $99,271, fades in above its empty bar
the bar fills to half its target

cues.word: qualifies for half the maximum funding
cues.why: the caption, Half the target qualifies for half the share
the bar fills to the whole target
the bar stops at its ceiling and the caption turns to The share is the ceiling

scenes.text: Before the Chancellor's Office releases any funding, your college needs to meet three conditions: name a CPL coordinator in map, confirm your participation, and upload Joint Services Transcripts for at least seventy-five percent of enrolled veterans. Until then, the funding is held in reserve for the two-year period.

cues.why: the heading, Meet the minimum conditions by December 30, 2026
the first condition, a CPL coordinator assigned and listed in MAP and on the landing page
the second condition, local confirmation of participation on file
the third condition, at least 75% of enrolled veterans’ Joint Services Transcripts uploaded in MAP
the closing line, the funding your college demonstrates is held in reserve for it

scenes.text: The Chancellor's Office will release funding twice a year, based on your college's CPL to date. The full two-year amount is available from year one, and what remains carries forward to year two.

cues.word: The Chancellor's Office will release funding
cues.why: the heading, Funding arrives in stages
the release dates, Feb 2027 Release 1 through Jun 2028 Release 4
the line, The full two-year amount is available from year one
the line, What remains after year one carries forward to year two for your college

scenes.text: You won't do this alone. Every priority comes with recommended strategies, a CPL Initiative help team supports every college, and detailed guidance will follow.

cues.why: the heading, You won’t do this alone

cues.word: Every priority comes with recommended strategies
cues.why: the kicker, Recommended strategies under every priority, and the strategies scrolling beneath it
the line, A CPL Initiative help team supports every college
the line, Detailed guidance will follow

scenes.text: Find details on the CPL funding page and let's do this together. Our time is now!
